body:
Thank you for raising this and documenting FrenzyMath’s contribution.

Based on the available public records, **Qin et al.’s formalization is the earlier implementation**:

- Their paper-pinned `v0.1.3` source, commit [`7a48598d…`](https://github.com/qinz1yang/differential-geometry/commit/7a48598d35109aa99d1cc678e2724c213cdf4ff3), is dated **September 27, 2026, at 08:15:33 UTC**. Their [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.33842) was submitted later that day.
- FrenzyMath’s [September 28 announcement](https://frenzymath.com/news/poincare-formalization/) explicitly acknowledges that Qin et al.’s formalization had already been released with a public full build. FrenzyMath’s [published verification record](https://github.com/frenzymath/Poincare-Conjecture/blob/main/archive/PoincareConjecture/references/ricci-flow/mapher/integration-verification/verification.json) records Comparator completion on **September 28, 2026, at 21:13:31 UTC**. Its claim to earlier Comparator verification is a distinct milestone.

The current candidate’s formalization is marked **“Lean verified” on [MathDB](https://mathdb.com/p/316224#s8)**. The verified source is the [MathDB-specific fork at `9f65eaf9…`](https://github.com/liao9yuan/differential-geometry-mathdb/tree/9f65eaf95b9ff5f1b39cfb2d2d24e51aed891568), with entry point [`Submission.solution : Problem.Target`](https://github.com/liao9yuan/differential-geometry-mathdb/blob/9f65eaf95b9ff5f1b39cfb2d2d24e51aed891568/Submission.lean).

That fork adapts the existing Qin et al. formalization to MathDB’s frozen target and verifier requirements, including a backported bridge and compatibility adjustments. **Its October commit date is the date of the verification adapter, not the original formalization’s completion date**, and does not reset the underlying work’s priority.

The evidence presented in this issue therefore does not establish grounds to change the current priority ordering. If you have other objections—for example, an earlier complete public FrenzyMath version, a specific gap in Qin et al.’s original release, or an attribution concern—please identify the relevant commits and supporting evidence so that those points can be reviewed directly.

FrenzyMath’s contributions and any potential Exposition submission can also be considered separately from the Lean priority question.

Thank you for raising this and documenting FrenzyMath’s contribution.

As explained in our [previous response](https://github.com/TheJustinSunPrize/awards/issues/5582#issuecomment-6940675136), the available public records support Qin et al.’s earlier implementation. The later MathDB fork adapts that existing formalization for verification and does not reset the original work’s priority. FrenzyMath’s Comparator verification is a separate milestone.

No additional evidence or specific objection has been provided since that response. On the evidence currently presented, we see no basis to change the current candidate’s priority ordering and are closing this issue. This closes the present objection; it does not constitute final award confirmation.

If you have further evidence of an earlier complete public version, a specific proof gap, or an attribution issue, please provide the relevant commits and supporting records so the matter can be reconsidered. Any Exposition submission can be assessed separately under the applicable process.
